pages.summary: Nonstiff ODE solvers for other tolerances: lower order for loose ones, higher order or multistep for tight ones.
body: They take the inputs and give the outputs of `ode45`. `ode23` (Bogacki-Shampine, orders 3 and 2) is cheapest at loose tolerances; `ode78` and `ode89` (Verner's pairs, orders 8 and 9) take few, long steps at tight tolerances; `ode113` (Adams-Bashforth-Moulton, orders 1 to 12) uses two evaluations a step, for problems whose function is costly. For stiff problems, the stiff solvers.

examples.title: Steps and errors at a tight tolerance
examples.intro: The orbit-like system y'' = -y over five periods, its exact solution cos(t), at RelTol 1e-10.
examples.output:
ode23   28441 steps  error 2.6e-09
ode45    3968 steps  error 3.8e-10
ode113    311 steps  error 7.5e-11
ode78     776 steps  error 1.8e-10
ode89     352 steps  error 2.9e-11

pages.summary: Stiff ODE solvers: for problems with very different time scales, where explicit solvers crawl.
body: In a stiff problem a fast component decays almost at once but forces an explicit solver to take tiny steps for stability. These implicit solvers take steps sized for the accuracy wanted. `ode15s` (numerical differentiation formulas of orders 1 to 5) is the first to try, and solves differential-algebraic systems with a singular mass matrix; `ode23s` (Rosenbrock) suits loose tolerances; `ode23t` (trapezoidal rule) moderately stiff problems; `ode23tb` (TR-BDF2) loose tolerances on stiff ones.

examples.title: A stiff equation: steps taken
examples.intro: y' = -1000(y - cos t): y follows cos t after a quick start, and an explicit solver stays held to steps near 1/1000.

examples.title: Robertson's chemical kinetics
examples.intro: Three species reacting at rates from 0.04 to 3e7: a classic stiff test, solved over 40 seconds.

pages.summary: Implicit ODEs and DAEs, F(t, y, y') = 0, and consistent initial values for them.
body: `ode15i` solves a system given as `F(t, y, yp)` returning a column of residuals: an implicit ODE, or a differential-algebraic system of index 1. Its start needs both `y0` and `yp0` with `F(t0, y0, yp0) = 0`; `decic` finds such values, holding the components marked 1 in `fixed_y0` and `fixed_yp0` and changing the others as little as it can.
syntax: [y0new, yp0new] = decic(odefun, t0, y0, fixed_y0, yp0, fixed_yp0)
[t, y] = ode15i(odefun, tspan, y0, yp0, options)

examples.title: y' + y^2 = 0 written implicitly
examples.intro: With y(0) = 1, decic finds y'(0) = -1; the exact solution is 1/(1 + t).

pages.summary: Options for the ODE solvers, made and read.
body: `odeset` takes names and values (`'RelTol'` 1e-3 and `'AbsTol'` 1e-6 unless set; `'MaxStep'`, `'InitialStep'`, `'Events'`, `'Jacobian'`, `'Mass'`, `'NonNegative'`, `'OutputFcn'`, `'Refine'`, `'MaxOrder'`, ...), or changes an existing structure. `odeget` reads one, with a default when it is not set. An events function `[value, isterminal, direction] = events(t, y)` marks where `value` crosses zero, and with `isterminal` 1 stops the solution there.

examples.title: A ball dropped from 10 m, stopped when it lands
examples.intro: The event is the height crossing zero going down; [t, y, te, ye, ie] gives when and where.
examples.code:
opts = odeset('RelTol', 1e-8, 'Events', @(t, y) deal(y(1), 1, -1));
[t, y, te, ye] = ode45(@(t, y) [y(2); -9.81], [0 5], [10; 0], opts);
te
sqrt(2*10/9.81)
ye(2)
odeget(opts, 'RelTol')
odeget(opts, 'MaxStep', 0.5)

pages.summary: The output function that plots the solution against time as the solver goes.
body: Given as `'OutputFcn'`, it plots each component (or those `'OutputSel'` names) as the steps come; a solver called with no outputs uses it, so `ode45(f, tspan, y0)` alone plots the solution.
syntax: As an output function; a solver called with no outputs, `ode45(odefun, tspan, y0)`, uses it too.

pages.summary: A solution structure evaluated at new times, and carried on to a later time.
body: `sol = ode45(...)` keeps the steps and the interpolant between them; `deval(sol, t)` evaluates it anywhere in the interval, a column for each time (and the derivative for the BVP and DDE solvers). `odextend` continues the solution past its end from where it stopped.
syntax: Carried on to `tfinal` (`[]` for the same function).

examples.title: Evaluated between steps, then carried on

pages.summary: An initial value problem as an object: its function, start and solver; solved by solve.
body: `F = ode(ODEFcn=@(t, y) ..., InitialValue=y0)` holds the problem; properties set the start time, parameters, tolerances, a Jacobian or mass matrix, and the solver (`'auto'`, `'nonstiff'`, `'stiff'`, or a solver's name; `SelectedSolver` says which). `solve(F, t0, tf)` gives the solution, `S.Time` a row and `S.Solution` a column for each time; `solutionFcn(F, t0, tf)` a function of time from the solver's interpolant.
syntax: With more properties; `S = solve(F, t0, tf)` gives its solution.

examples.title: A decay with a parameter

pages.summary: Boundary value problems y' = f(x, y) on [a, b], with conditions at both ends, by collocation.
body: `odefun(x, y)` gives y' as a column; `bcfun(ya, yb)` the residuals of the boundary conditions, zero when they hold. The guess from `bvpinit` gives the first mesh, refined until the residual is within `'RelTol'` on each interval. `bvp4c` uses fourth-order collocation, `bvp5c` fifth-order (more accurate on a mesh). Unknown parameters can be solved for alongside. The solution has `x`, `y` and `yp` on the final mesh, and `deval` gives values between.

examples.title: y'' = -y with y(0) = 0 and y(π/2) = 1, whose solution is sin(x)

pages.summary: First guesses for the boundary value solvers: from a mesh and values, or from a solution carried to a longer interval.
body: `bvpinit(xmesh, yinit)` gives the first mesh and a guess on it: a constant column, or a function `yinit(x)`; a third input guesses unknown parameters. `bvpinit(sol, [anew bnew])` and `bvpxtend(sol, xnew)` start a longer interval from a solution, its end values carried out (by the slope, for `bvpxtend`).
syntax: From a solution, to new ends.
From a solution, past an end.

examples.title: A guess, and a solution carried on

pages.summary: Options of the boundary value solvers, made and read.
body: The names: `'RelTol'` (1e-3) and `'AbsTol'` (1e-6), `'NMax'` (the most mesh points), `'SingularTerm'` (S, for y' = S·y/x + f), `'FJacobian'`, `'BCJacobian'`, `'Stats'` and `'Vectorized'`.

pages.summary: Delay differential equations: y' depends on y at earlier times.
body: `dde23` solves y'(t) = f(t, y(t), Z) where `Z(:, j)` is y(t - lags(j)) for constant positive lags; `history` gives y before the start (a constant, a function of t, or an earlier solution). It steps on to the points where a lag carries the jump at the start forward. `ddesd` takes delays that depend on t and y: `delays(t, y)` gives the times at which y is taken. `ddeset` and `ddeget` make and read their options (`'RelTol'`, `'AbsTol'`, `'Events'`, `'InitialY'`, `'Jumps'`, ...). The solution goes to `deval`.
syntax: sol = dde23(ddefun, lags, history, tspan, options)

examples.title: Delayed feedback: y'(t) = -y(t - 1)
A delay that grows with time

pages.summary: Parabolic and elliptic PDEs in one space variable and time, solved by the method of lines; and the solution between mesh points.
body: The equations are c·∂u/∂t = x^(-m)·∂/∂x(x^m·f) + s, with `[c, f, s] = pdefun(x, t, u, dudx)` and m 0 (slab), 1 (cylinder) or 2 (sphere). `icfun(x)` gives the start; `[pl, ql, pr, qr] = bcfun(xl, ul, xr, ur, t)` the boundary conditions p + q·f = 0 at each end (q = 0 holds u). `sol(i, j, k)` is component k at `tspan(i)` and `xmesh(j)`; `pdeval` interpolates one time's solution between the mesh points.
syntax: sol = pdepe(m, pdefun, icfun, bcfun, xmesh, tspan)
Between mesh points, with the slope.
